note: 034 — brief lines that FAIL verification (CLAUDE.md, V26: armed BEFORE the take). Any caption matching a `bad` pattern means the take was read from the BRIEF: the master is blocked until it is re-recorded or accepted. Read with JSON.parse, never regex over source. fixes.brief: This year, his salary is two million.
fixes.briefSpoken: This year, his salary is 2 million.
fixes.use: This year, he's paid two million.
fixes.why: His contractual salary is $70M a year, $68M of it deferred (AP, 11 Dec 2023; Cot's). 'His salary is two million' can be answered with 'no, it's seventy'; 'he's paid two million' is exactly true.

fixes.brief: Call it four hundred sixty million, not seven hundred.
fixes.use: That's about four hundred sixty million, not seven hundred.
fixes.why: $460M is baseball's luxury-tax value (10 x $46.08M); the players' union calculated $437.8M (Cot's). 'Call it' presents it as THE present value; 'That's about', after 'for its luxury tax, baseball values', keeps it tied to the tax (the brief's guardrail).

fixes.brief: And Sportico estimates he makes a hundred twenty-five million a year off the field.
fixes.briefSpoken: And Sportico estimates he makes 125 million a year off the field.
fixes.use: And Sportico estimates he'll make a hundred twenty-five million off the field this year.
fixes.why: Sportico (17 Mar 2026): $125M projected for 2026, a record (last year: $100M), not a steady yearly amount.

guardrails.why: The $700 million is real and will all be paid: never say or show that he loses money, or that the contract is fake (the brief).
~$460M is baseball's luxury-tax present value: never present it as his actual pay (the brief).
